name: Authentication & Passwords
description: Password security, biometrics, multi-factor and passwordless authentication (FIDO/WebAuthn).
narrative:
The earliest listed work at USENIX Security wrestled mainly with the stubborn realities of text passwords: why people pick weak ones, how they forget them, and whether organizational nudges help. Studies like "Better managed than memorized? Studying the Impact of Managers on Password Strength and Reuse" (2018) and "Forgetting of Passwords: Ecological Theory and Data" (2018) treated passwords as a human-factors problem, while "The Rewards and Costs of Stronger Passwords in a University" (2018) measured the real tradeoffs of strict policies at scale. In parallel, researchers began protecting the password ecosystem itself, with "Simple Password-Hardened Encryption Services" (2018) hardening stored secrets against server compromise.

A clear shift came in 2019 toward defending against breaches and reuse at internet scale. "Protecting accounts from credential stuffing with password breach alerting" (2019) introduced privacy-preserving ways to warn users that their credentials had leaked, and "Birthday, Name and Bifacial-security: Understanding Passwords of Chinese Web Users" (2019) broadened the field beyond English-speaking users. By 2021, breach detection itself became a research target through decoy-based schemes like "Using Amnesia to Detect Credential Database Breaches" (2021).

The next wave moved past passwords entirely. Biometrics matured with "Liveness is Not Enough: Enhancing Fingerprint Authentication with Behavioral Biometrics to Defeat Puppet Attacks" (2020) and the more exploratory "Inexpensive Brainwave Authentication" (2021), while the community tackled the deployment and usability of second factors in "Empirical Measurement of Systemic 2FA Usability" (2020) and "Driving 2FA Adoption at Scale" (2021). These papers reframed authentication as a system-wide adoption and human-experience problem rather than a pure cryptographic one.

By 2023 the area had split into sharper specialties. A cluster of machine-learning attack papers, including "Improving Real-world Password Guessing Attacks via Bi-directional Transformers" (2023), "Password Guessing Using Random Forest" (2023), and "Pass2Edit: A Multi-Step Generative Model for Guessing Edited Passwords" (2023), pushed guessing attacks to new strength, prompting careful re-evaluation of defenses in "No Single Silver Bullet: Measuring the Accuracy of Password Strength Meters" (2023). At the same time, "A Study of Multi-Factor and Risk-Based Authentication Availability" (2023) audited how widely stronger authentication is actually offered. The arc runs from understanding and patching passwords, through breach defense and second factors, toward biometrics, ML-driven attacks, and the broader question of whether and how multi-factor authentication reaches real users.
